summary: Okta attribute deprecation causes partial RBAC grant for Feature-Flag Console
description: Issue summary: After Okta IDP started deprecating the 'location' custom attribute used in our SCIM to RBAC mapping, a subset of engineers can no longer see or toggle flags in the Feature-Flag Console. Impact: ~12 engineers in product and QA report missing 'feature-flag-admin' permissions while the same users retain other console permissions. This blocks scheduled canary rollouts and a hotfix deployment.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) User signs in to Feature-Flag Console via Okta SSO in prod-us-west. 2) Post-login, service evaluates SCIM-provided attributes and maps to RBAC roles. 3) If 'location' attribute is absent or mapped to 'N/A' the role mapping path erroneously skips secondaryGroup assignment. 4) Observe that 'feature-flag-admin' checkbox is not present in the UI and API returns 403 for /api/v1/flags/:id/toggle.
observed_behavior: Affected users authenticate successfully but receive 403s when attempting toggle API and do not see admin controls in UI. Audit logs show successful SCIM patch with 'location' set to '-' or omitted. RBAC service logs note 'group mapping fallback missed' for these identities.
expected_behavior: When the IDP deprecates an attribute, SCIM and RBAC should fall back to alternate attributes (e.g., 'department' or Okta groups) and preserve existing role grants until an explicit change is made by the admin.
logs_and_traces:
- Feature-Flag Console auth trace (auth-trace-2026-03-11-14:22): shows SCIM->RBAC mapping call returned 200 but mapping result omitted secondaryGroups array.
- RBAC service warn: 'mapping:secondaryGroup not found, no fallback configured' at 14:22:05 UTC.
- Okta SCIM audit (okta-audit-2026-03-11): entries show attribute 'location' marked deprecated in metadata and some userProfile patches containing 'location': null.
impact_summary: Operational: scheduled canary toggles for release 2026.03.11 blocked; Team productivity: ~12 engineers impacted; Security/compliance: no escalation required but role inconsistency could confuse access reviews.
workaround: Manual grant: Admins can temporarily assign 'feature-flag-admin' to affected users via the console user management page. We documented a one-off script (scripts/grant_flag_admin.sh) to mass-assign rights during the incident window.
investigation_notes:
- Hypothesis A: SCIM connector removed 'location' from user payload after an Okta schema cleanup.
- Hypothesis B: RBAC mapping code treats an empty string or '-' as a sentinel to remove secondaryGroup assignment.
- Verified: SCIM connector code (commit: github.com/redwood-inference/scim-connector@b2d4f9e) changed handling of null attributes two weeks ago; no fallback mapping was added.
- Coco (oncall-auth) reproduced locally by setting user.profile.location to null and observed identical 403s.
- Related tickets: INT-202406 (group-encoding mismatch) contains notes about mapping fallbacks; INT-531246 mentions SCIM rate limit but not relevant.
comments: Aisha Patel (Reporter) - 2026-03-10: Noticed several engineers can't toggle flags during morning deploy. They authenticate fine, but UI is missing admin controls.
Miguel Ortega (Assignee) - 2026-03-10: I can reproduce with a test account by clearing 'location' on the Okta profile. Adding logs and routing to auth team to confirm SCIM payloads.

Jules Park (Auth Eng) - 2026-03-11: Confirmed SCIM connector updated handling of nulls in commit b2d4f9e; we didn't add a fallback mapping. Proposing quick patch to RBAC mapper to check Okta 'groups' list before dropping secondaryGroup.
Samira Chen (SRE) - 2026-03-11: Deployed temporary admin-script to grant rights to the affected list; recording in runbook. Will coordinate with SOC for audit trail.
Miguel Ortega - 2026-03-12: Patch prepared: rbac-mapper now treats missing 'location' as non-fatal and consults 'groups' -> PR #1237 opened. Running canary for 2 users in prod-us-west.
resolution: In progress: PR #1237 for rbac-mapper fallback behavior created and under code review. Temporary mass-grant script used for immediate unblock. Final resolution will include adding unit tests and a rolling deploy, then coordination with Identity team to update SCIM connector behavior.
